title: Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs)
subtitle: Fractional unitholding in highways, power transmission grids, and telecom towers
summary: InvITs aggregate long-term income-generating infrastructure assets like toll roads and electrical transmission lines, distributing long-duration cash flows to unitholders.

sources.name: National Stock Exchange of India - InvIT Category Overview

disclaimer: Educational information only. Not investment advice. TradeOne is not a SEBI-registered investment adviser. Rules, taxes and yields change; verify with official sources.

sections.title: What is an InvIT?
sections.content: An Infrastructure Investment Trust (InvIT) is an investment vehicle that pools money from investors to own and operate completed or revenue-generating national infrastructure assets. In India, public InvITs primarily own assets like power transmission lines, operational toll highways, and gas pipelines with contractual or toll-based cash inflows.
sections.analogy: Think of an InvIT like a community toll booth or power line. Every time vehicles travel on the expressway or electricity flows through the transmission network, a tariff or toll is paid. After maintenance costs, the surplus cash is distributed to the unitholders.

sections.title: How Investors Earn from InvITs
sections.content: Unitholders receive returns through regular cash flows and unit price movements:
points: Cash Distributions: SEBI mandates that at least 90% of Net Distributable Cash Flows (NDCF) must be paid out to unitholders periodically (semi-annually or quarterly).
Unit Market Price: As traffic counts rise, tariff rates adjust with inflation indices, or debt is paid down, unit values on exchanges can fluctuate.

sections.title: What are the Risks?
sections.content: Infrastructure assets have long life cycles but face distinct operational risks:
points: Traffic or Volume Risk: For toll roads, alternate highway routes or fuel price spikes can reduce vehicular volume.
Concession Life Expiry: Many toll roads are held under Concession Agreements with NHAI for 20-30 years, after which ownership reverts to the government. Terminal value amortizes over time.
Regulatory & Tariff Risks: Changes in state electricity tariffs or interstate wheeling charges can influence cash flow margins.
Interest Rate Risk: High capital expenditure requires debt servicing; higher interest rates increase borrowing costs.

sections.title: Who Often Considers InvITs?
sections.content: Investors seeking higher cash yield profiles (often 7% to 8.5% historically) with long-term sovereign or public utility counterparties such as NHAI or state power transmission utilities.

sections.title: Worked Example (Sample Illustration)
sections.content: Suppose an investor purchases 1,000 units of a public InvIT at ₹100 per unit (total investment: ₹1,00,000).
details: Annual distribution per unit: ₹7.80 (paid across the financial year).
Distribution split may include interest, return of capital, and dividend as specified on the credit statement.

sections.title: Tax Overview in Plain English
sections.content: Similar to REITs, distributions arrive categorized into interest, dividend, and capital repayment components:
points: Interest component is taxed at the investor's marginal slab rate.
Dividend component is tax-exempt if the SPV opted for the Section 115BAA concessional corporate tax scheme, or taxed at slab rate otherwise.

Capital gains on exchange transfer: LTCG at 12.5% for holding periods over 12 months (on gains above ₹1.25 lakh total across eligible equity/units); STCG at 20% for holding periods of 12 months or less.

sections.title: How to Buy InvIT Units
steps: Search for public InvIT tickers on NSE/BSE using your regular stockbroker terminal (e.g., PGINVIT for PowerGrid InvIT, IRBInvIT).
Enter quantity (minimum lot size is 1 unit for publicly traded InvITs).
Execute transaction at prevailing market price. Units credit to your Demat account under T+1 settlement.

items.myth: InvIT units are identical to ordinary equity shares of construction firms.
items.fact: Construction firms take on execution and raw material risks. InvITs typically hold finished, operational assets that already collect revenue.

items.myth: The unit price of an InvIT will grow indefinitely like a fast-growing tech stock.
items.fact: Because concession agreements for roads have finite durations, capital amortizes. InvIT returns are predominantly driven by cash payouts rather than rapid capital growth.

terms.definition: The contractual duration granted by a government authority to operate the asset and collect tolls.
Assets like power grids that receive revenue as long as lines are kept active, regardless of power throughput.
